verdict.rationale: Flagsmith ships its own background automation for flag changes. Release Pipelines move flags through stages automatically using triggers and actions, and can auto-generate change requests. Scheduled Flags queue changes that apply automatically at a set future time, but that is a one-off action, not a recurring schedule. Running the MCP server 'fully automated in a CI/CD pipeline' relies on the host CI platform, so it earns no credit. missing for 10: recurring or cron-style schedules, automation beyond flag rollout and release workflows, agent-driven autonomous background tasks native to the product, independent or hands-on corroboration of Release Pipelines working.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
The scheduled change will be queued and applied automatically at the specified time.
